title: Scatter Plots and Overplotting Remediation
description: Visualizing relationships between two continuous variables and resolving heavy overplotting.
conditions: Two continuous variables with potential linear, non-linear, or cluster relationships
Large sample size (N > 5,000) causing extreme point occlusion and solid dark blobs
recommended_methods: Alpha transparency adjustment (e.g. alpha = 0.1 to 0.3) for moderate N
2D Hexagonal Binning (Hexbin) or 2D Density Contours for large N (> 10,000)
Linear regression or LOESS trend line overlay with 95% confidence interval band
selection_rules: If N > 10,000 points, do not plot raw scatter dots; use Hexbin plot with logarithmic color scale
Always include an annotated Pearson r or Spearman rho value directly on the plot
If adding a third variable, encode via color palette, reserving size encoding only for natural volume metrics
limitations: Hexbin plots lose visibility of isolated extreme outlier points (overlay single red points for outliers)
LOESS trend lines overfit locally if span parameter is set too small
source: Cleveland (1985) The Elements of Graphing Data
